newsitem.title: GERMANY: INSTANT VIEW - German July unemployment rises.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - German July unemployment rises.

text.p: Following are economists' reactions to news pan-German joblessness rose a seasonally adjusted 17,000 from June. The unadjusted jobless rate rose to 11.4 percent from 11.0 percent, the Federal Labour Office said.
Gerhard Grebe, Bank Julius Baer, Frankfurt:

"The rise in unemployment is as expected for July, because this if the first month after the end of a quarter. There are always some layoffs in such a month, some contracts running out, and schools are out.

"The worsening of the situation in the east reflects the construction industry and the curtailing of jobs-creation measures. In the West, the situation is improving with an pick-up in economic activity and the end of corporate restructuring."
"We have to focus on the Western figures, which show a turning point on the labour market.
"In the west, the economy is growing strong enough to create more jobs. In the east, it is not a cyclical problem, it is structural, it is a question of how much more can be done to create jobs.
"There are a lot of structural problems in west Germany as well, but unemployment is not rising in west Germany for now."
Guenter Redeker, Chase Investment Bank, London:
"This is much weaker than originally expected. The east German construction sector is suffering a lot, though the west German economy is gaining a little momentum.
"To call this a turning point is a heroic statement. The failure of the tax reform process will be a big negative for investment."
"The figures are disappointing. It is not unusual in a holiday month that unemployment is rising, but we thought the seasonally adjusted numbers would show a decline.
"Industrial production and orders data earlier this week point to a strengthening of the economy, and we think this will lead to a turnaround."
